name: agent-harness
description: A project-agnostic harness for agentic coding: a gate-line protocol with a committed baseline, PreToolUse guards, a doc contract, a context budget and a track/handoff lifecycle. Zero dependencies.
//: ZERO DEPENDENCIES, AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING. `dependencies` and `devDependencies` are written
out as empty objects on purpose, so the property is a line in this file and not an absence.
The harness is copied INTO the repo it grades and runs from a PreToolUse hook on a fresh clone,
before anyone has installed anything: a helper that needs a package is a guard that is silently
off on exactly that clone. It is also why CI has no install step and no lockfile to drift.
`node bin/harness.js --self-test` asserts both objects are empty, and CI asserts it again.
`test` and `gates` must read exactly what scripts/harness/common.json `packageScripts` says:
scripts/harness/branch-sync.js compares the two. `gates:check` is the same check with the
tolerated skips DERIVED from harness.config.json and the committed baseline instead of typed.
`test` is `node --test` with NO PATH, and that is measured, not style. `engines` says >=20, and
no path spelling works on both sides of Node 21: a quoted glob ("tests/**/*.test.js") is not
understood before it and exits `Could not find`, while a bare directory (tests/) is read as a
module from it on and reported as one failing test. With no path every supported version
finds the *.test.js files itself, and finds the same ones.
`files` is what an installed copy needs and nothing else. gates.json and the red logs are one
machine's run output; the agents and skills are listed one by one so a third-party skill
sitting in a working checkout can never be published by a directory glob.
